config.description: The configuration file, and whether it was read.

cwd.description: The working directory the checks used.

problems.description: Everything that would stop a run, per provider where it is about one.

ready.description:
Whether a run can go ahead: at least one provider is ready and no
problem is about the whole system. The exit status is 0 when it is true
and 1 when it is false.

skills.description: The skills built into this executable.

oneOf.description: Every run with this provider.
Only runs that grant exact commands (`permissions.commands`).
Only runs in the `build` permission mode.
Runs still start, but each would report its cleanup as not confirmed.

No run is refused or changed. It is a warning: the provider did not
answer `--version`, which a run records only as an absent version.

CommandHook.description:
Whether the Claude Code version has the blocking hook interface that exact
command grants need.

available.description:
Whether the installed version is that release or later, as a run
decides it.

required_version.description: The oldest release that has it.

ConfigReport.description:
The user-level configuration file: where it is looked for and what came of
it. No value from the file is in the report, only the names of the keys it
sets and counts.

found.description: Whether something exists at the path, usable or not.

path.description:
The path the file is looked for at, or null when there is no place to
look (no `DELEGA_CONFIG`, no absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME`).

read.description:
Whether the file was read and is in effect. A file that is found and
refused is a problem, and nothing from it is applied.

settings.description: The keys the file sets, as dotted names such as `defaults.model`.

DenyFile.description: A settings file that was read, and how many deny rules it held.

rules.description: The rules in the file, before deduplication.

DenyInfo.description:
The deny rules a Claude run would apply, as a run's notes give them: files
and counts, never a rule.

applied.description: Rules a worker would receive, after deduplication.

files.description: The settings files that exist and were read, with their rule counts.

skipped.description: Existing local settings files that would be ignored, with the reason.

EnvCounts.description:
How many environment variables a worker would receive, by reason. No names
and no values.

base.description: Of the caller's: base variables (user, shell, locale and the like).

network.description: Of the caller's: proxy and certificate settings.

passed.description: Variables the worker would receive in all.

provider.description: Of the caller's: variables that belong to the provider.

set_by_delega.description: Variables delega sets itself for this provider.

withheld.description: Variables of the caller's environment that would not be passed.

Limits.description: The limits in force, from the constants the code uses.

ManagedFileCounts.description: The files of a source that is a directory, as counts. No file is named.

found.description:
Files found: `*.json` files that are not hidden in a drop-in directory,
or users' preferences files. Counting stops at a limit.

limit_reached.description:
For a directory, whether a limit on files, directory entries or bytes
stopped the scan before the directory was exhausted, or a file in it
changed size while it was read, so there may be more than `found` and
keys may be missing. For a single file, set when the file changed size
while it was read; there is no other file to find.

unreadable.description:
Of those, how many could not be read or parsed. Always 0 for
preferences, which are not opened.

ManagedKey.description: A key in a managed source that can change how a delega launch is honoured.

category.description:
What the key is about. Not what it does: no value is read, and what a
key does is for the provider's reference to say.

name.description:
The key's name, dotted when it is nested, such as `permissions.deny`.
Never its value.

ManagedKeyCategory.description:
What a managed key is about. It places the key; it says nothing about what
the key does on this system.

oneOf.description: Permission rules, working directories and what tools may touch.
Hooks.
MCP servers and the flags that configure them.
Plugins and other customization sources.
Sandboxing of commands.
Login, credentials and which service is used.
Environment variables.
Which models may be used.
Which provider versions may start.
How managed settings themselves are computed.
A key of Codex's `requirements.toml`.
A key of Codex's legacy `managed_config.toml`.

ManagedSource.description: A managed source that exists on this system.

files.description:
For a source that is a directory, how many files it holds. For a
single file it is null, with one exception: when the file changed size
while it was read it is one file found, one not read and
`limit_reached`, and the state is `partly_read`.

keys.description:
The keys in it that can affect a delega launch, by name, in the order of
the provider's table (Claude Code) or of the names (Codex). Every name
is one this build knows, never text from the file. For a directory, the
keys of all its files together. Empty when the source was not read or
sets none of them.

note.description:
What is known of the source that does not depend on a key in it. Fixed
text for the kind.

other_keys.description:
For a Codex file, how many of its top-level keys are in no table of
this build. They are counted and not named: such a key may be a typing
mistake Codex ignores, and its name is whatever the file says. 0 for
every other kind of source.

path.description:
The path of the file or directory. Always one of the fixed locations,
never a name read from a directory.

ManagedSourceKind.description: What kind of managed source a path is.

oneOf.description: Claude Code's `managed-settings.json`.

Claude Code's `managed-settings.d/` directory, as a whole: `path` is the
directory and `files` counts the `*.json` files in it.
Claude Code's `managed-mcp.json`.
Codex's `requirements.toml`.
Codex's legacy `managed_config.toml`.

The macOS managed preferences file of the provider's domain for the
whole system.

The macOS managed preferences files of the provider's domain in users'
directories, as a whole: `path` is the directory that holds the users'
directories and `files` counts the files.

ManagedSourceState.description: What doctor could do with a managed source.

oneOf.description: It was read and parsed, and `keys` lists what was found in it.

Not gone through completely. For a directory: some of its files could
not be read, or a limit stopped the scan (`files.limit_reached`), in
which case there may be files that were never looked at; `keys` lists
what was found in the files read. For a single file: its size changed
while it was read, so no key is reported from it.

It is there and could not be read or parsed, so nothing is known about
what it sets.
It is there and doctor does not open it (managed preferences).

ProcessInspection.description: Whether the process listing that confirms cleanup works.

available.description: Whether one listing, run now as cleanup runs it, gave a usable table.

detail.description: Why not, when it is not available. Free text; it names no process.

Provider.description: The provider CLI that runs the assignment.

oneOf.description: Claude Code.
Codex CLI.

ProviderCheck.description: What was found for one provider.

command_hook.description:
For Claude Code, whether the command hook interface is available. Null
for Codex, which has no minimum version.

deny_rules.description:
The deny rules a Claude run would apply. Null for Codex, which reads
none, and when the launch could not be built.

env.description:
The environment a worker would get, or null when the launch could not be
built.

executable.description: The executable a run would use, or null when none was found.

executable_source.description:
Where the lookup found it: the override variable's name, `config` (the
configuration file), `PATH`, or `option` when a library caller set
`ProviderOptions::executable`.

managed_settings.description:
The managed (administrator) settings sources found on this system for
the provider, with the names of the keys in them that can change how a
delega launch is honoured. Empty when none was found. They are a
notice: they are not problems and do not change `ready`.

ready.description: Whether no problem stops every run with this provider.

sandbox.description:
For Claude Code, the platform and `PATH` dependencies of the sandbox
`build` runs require, as checked. Null for Codex.

version.description:
The first non-blank line of `--version` output with credentials
removed, trimmed, and cut to 100 characters with `...` appended when
cut, or null when there was none.

ReportedProblem.description: A problem, with the provider it is about.

blocks.description:
What the problem stops: `run` (every run with the provider),
`command_grants` (only runs that grant exact commands), `build` (can stop
runs in the `build` permission mode; see the message), `cleanup`
(runs start, but cleanup cannot be confirmed) or `nothing` (a warning: no
run is refused).

kind.description:
A stable label, including `managed_mcp_exclusive` when managed MCP blocks
Claude runs. See [`Problem::kind`] and
[`PROCESS_INSPECTION_UNAVAILABLE`].

provider.description: The provider it is about, or null when it is about the whole system.

RunLimits.description: The defaults and bounds a single run has.

default_timeout_secs.description: The time limit when a request sets none, in seconds.

max_output_bytes.description: Most bytes of provider standard output kept.

max_stderr_bytes.description: Most bytes of provider standard error kept.

max_timeout_secs.description: The longest time limit a request may set, in seconds.

min_timeout_secs.description: The shortest time limit a request may set, in seconds.

version_probe_timeout_secs.description: How long the `--version` probe may take, in seconds.

SandboxCheck.description:
What doctor checks of the platform and `PATH` dependencies of Claude Code's
sandbox, which `build` runs require. It looks for files and starts nothing,
so it is not proof the sandbox starts: a kernel or security policy that
blocks user namespaces, for example, is not checked.

missing.description:
Those of `requires` not found on the worker's `PATH`. Relative and
empty entries are taken from the working directory.

requirements_met.description:
Whether the checked dependencies are met: on macOS always (Claude Code
uses the built-in Seatbelt framework), on Linux when every tool in
`requires` was found on the worker's `PATH`, elsewhere never (Claude
Code has no sandbox there). Other causes of a failed start are not
checked.

requires.description:
The executables looked for: `bwrap` and `socat` on Linux, none
elsewhere.

system.description: The system, as Rust names it: `macos`, `linux` or another.

SkillDigest.description: A packaged skill and its digest, as `delega version --output json` lists it.

digest.description: The SHA-256 digest of its text.

uri.description: Where an MCP client reads it.

SkippedFile.description: A local settings file that was not read, and why.

SupervisorLimits.description: The limits of the supervisor that serves the MCP tools.

default_wait_secs.description: The timeout `wait` uses when it gets none, in seconds.

max_outstanding_request_checks.description: Request checks that may be outstanding at once.

max_queued_per_worker.description: Runs waiting behind one worker's running run.

retained_bytes.description: Estimated bytes of finished results kept readable.

retention_secs.description: How long a finished result stays readable, in seconds.

wait_ceiling_secs.description: The longest one `wait` blocks, in seconds.
